cards.title: Adapt the Found–Matched–Chosen framework to AI search
cards.summary: Map three checkpoints — discoverability, factual query matching, and external reputation — onto a Shopify store's AI search readiness.
cards.use_when: Planning an AI search / GEO roadmap for a Shopify store and deciding which stage to fix first.
steps: Use Found (discoverability), Matched (factual product fit), and Chosen (reputation and relevance) as an audit checklist, not a verified AI ranking pipeline.

Stage 1 — Found: technical reading. Confirm pages aren't password-protected, robots.txt doesn't block AI agents, and content is server-rendered rather than injected by JS widgets. Also verify schema markup and eligibility for Shopify's global product catalog.

Stage 2 — Matched: content. Replace vague marketing copy with explicit, hard data facts (size, colour, use case) that an AI can filter against a query and place the product into its candidate shortlist.
Review independent customer feedback and product experiences to understand reputation; recommendation counts and selection methods vary by engine and query.
Work stages in order — a product that isn't found or matched can't be chosen, so fix crawlability and copy before investing in reputation building.
Note that the source presents this as a high-level mental model from a small research effort, not a validated ranking formula; treat stage importance as directional.
caveats: The framework is the presenter's own three-stage simplification; it has not been published as a verified ranking model.
Big brands still dominate broad queries; smaller stores should target specific, long-tail queries as in traditional SEO.
cards.source_name: Get Your Shopify Store AI-SEO-Ready in 5 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Check whether AI crawlers can actually access your store
cards.summary: Verify robots.txt and run a crawler-style fetch to confirm AI agents can reach your Shopify pages.
cards.use_when: Auditing a Shopify store's crawlability before any AI search content work, or diagnosing why an AI tool can't describe a product.
steps: Open the store's robots.txt by appending /robots.txt to the domain and scan for rules that disallow major AI agents. Shopify auto-generates this file, so problems usually come from manual edits or apps that added rules.
Do a quick sanity check that common agent user-agents are not blocked or disallowed.
Fetch a public product URL with a crawler user-agent as a diagnostic; compare the HTTP response and returned content with robots.txt rules and server logs.
Use actual fetch results and crawler documentation to investigate access; an assistant claiming access is not verification.
Remove password protection from pages that should be publicly indexed and confirm pages aren't only reachable through client-side navigation.
Re-check robots.txt after installing apps, since apps can modify the auto-generated file. Verify the current Shopify robots.txt UI and Sidekick behaviour, as interfaces change.
caveats: A spoofed user-agent fetch does not prove a real crawler can access the site or that it is indexed. Robots.txt compliance, network controls, and crawler purpose differ.
Enable only crawlers consistent with the store owner's policy; training crawlers and search crawlers are not interchangeable.
cards.source_name: Get Your Shopify Store AI-SEO-Ready in 5 Minutes.docx

cards.title: See your product page the way a JS-blind crawler sees it
cards.summary: Compare initial HTML with rendered product content to identify crawler-dependent visibility gaps.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing whether reviews, FAQs or spec content on a Shopify product page is invisible to AI crawlers.
steps: Open the product page in a browser, disable JavaScript, then reload the page.
Compare the initial HTML and normal rendered page; missing specs, FAQs, or reviews identify dependence on JavaScript, not proof of invisibility to every engine.
Treat leftover placeholders or snippet stubs where the content should be as a red flag — the agent sees a shell, not the data.
Fix by moving critical content into server-rendered areas: theme templates, metafields rendered in Liquid, or app blocks that render on load rather than lazy widgets.
Prioritise the content that drives AI matching — sizing, materials, colour, use cases, and review sentiment — rather than decorative elements.
Retest after theme or app changes. For Google, use URL Inspection to inspect rendered HTML; Google can render JavaScript, while other crawlers vary.
caveats: Shopify themes and apps update their rendering behaviour; verify current behaviour on each page type rather than assuming a widget is always JS-only.
Not every missing element matters — only content an AI needs to match or justify a recommendation.
cards.source_name: Get Your Shopify Store AI-SEO-Ready in 5 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Publish factual product attributes for specific shopper queries
cards.summary: Help search systems match products to explicit customer requirements.
cards.use_when: Improving ecommerce product discoverability and accurate product matching in search.
steps: Replace vague product copy with verified material, colour, dimensions, capacity, compatibility and use-case facts.
Keep titles, descriptions, variant fields and metafields consistent; remove stale app metadata after review.
Map a specific shopper query to the attributes on the product page and check that each claimed match is supported.
caveats: This is a readiness check, not a guarantee of ranking or AI recommendations. Verify current platform requirements before implementation.
cards.source_name: Get Your Shopify Store AI-SEO-Ready in 5 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Audit Shopify catalog readiness alongside storefront SEO
cards.summary: Treat backend catalog data and storefront crawlability as separate distribution checks.
cards.use_when: Improving ecommerce product discoverability and accurate product matching in search.
steps: Check current Shopify catalog eligibility and channel settings in the merchant admin or official documentation; use Sidekick for navigation assistance.
Review product titles, descriptions, valid prices, availability and metafields for completeness and accuracy.
Compare backend catalog records with visible product details and correct discrepancies.
caveats: This is a readiness check, not a guarantee of ranking or AI recommendations. Verify current platform requirements before implementation.
cards.source_name: Get Your Shopify Store AI-SEO-Ready in 5 Minutes.docx

cards.title: Validate product structured data against visible store facts
cards.summary: Make product facts machine-readable without inventing schema claims.
cards.use_when: Improving ecommerce product discoverability and accurate product matching in search.
steps: Inspect Product structured data on representative product and variant pages.
Validate the markup with the applicable validator and compare price, availability and product identity with visible content.
Correct theme or app conflicts and recheck after changes.
caveats: This is a readiness check, not a guarantee of ranking or AI recommendations. Verify current platform requirements before implementation.
